finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /users lets any anonymous caller enumerate id and name of users in any org by supplying an arbitrary org value.
finding.sink: SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1 (db.js:9), response via res.json(rows) (db.js:10)

trace.note: GET /users route registered with no auth middleware
req.query.org used directly as bind parameter with no org-membership check
all matching rows returned as JSON, no LIMIT or pagination
app.listen(3002) binds all interfaces by default, making route network-reachable

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query ($1) prevents SQL injection but not authorization; no authentication middleware in this file; no org-membership or ownership check; no pagination or row limit. Precondition: no auth applied outside this file (only db.js exists in the directory). Severity drops if an authenticating gateway fronts the app.

verdict.guard_found: none. db.js:8 registers GET /users with no auth middleware. db.js:9 binds req.query.org directly as $1, which blocks SQL injection but is not an authorization check. db.js:10 returns all rows with no LIMIT. No other files exist in the directory to add a gateway or middleware.
verdict.reason: The route at db.js:8-10 is unauthenticated and returns id and name for any org value taken from req.query.org, and the only listener at db.js:23 is a standalone app on port 3002 with no authorization control in the code; the one caveat is that an external gateway not visible in this directory could front it, which would lower severity but not refute the flaw in the code.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /count discloses the line count of data.csv in the process working directory to anonymous callers, and each request spawns a process with no rate limiting.
finding.source: Incoming HTTP request to GET /count (db.js:19); no attacker input reaches command arguments

trace.note: GET /count route with no auth middleware
execFile runs wc -l on fixed filename data.csv relative to cwd
stdout sent to client; error argument e ignored so failures return empty 200

finding.guards_checked: execFile without shell and with fixed arguments prevents command injection. No authentication or rate limiting. Precondition: data.csv is sensitive enough that its row count matters. Severity low.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /count route (db.js:19-21) has no auth middleware, and the file has no app.use or rate limiting. A grep of the directory for app.use, authenticate, requireAuth, and rate-limit found nothing. execFile (db.js:20) takes a fixed argument array with no shell, so command injection is not possible, but that does not block the disclosure.
verdict.reason: The GET /count route at db.js:19 has no authentication, and db.js:20 runs execFile("wc", ["-l", "data.csv"]) and sends stdout to the anonymous caller via res.send(out), so the row count of data.csv is disclosed. The severity is low, and the impact depends on whether that row count is sensitive.
